title: [LPLB] Make the IPM solver CUDA-graph safe, and halve its shared memory
body:
Two related changes to LPLB's single-block IPM solver. The second needs the first: sizing the LP for the worst case makes shared memory the binding constraint, and the fused kernel is what keeps the worst case in budget.

---

## 1. Fuse `ax2` into the syrk

The kernel staged `ax2 = A X²` into an `NC × NV` shared-memory array purely to feed two cuBLASDx GEMMs. `X` is diagonal, so `ax2a = A X² Aᵀ` and `ax2c = A X² c` can both be accumulated in one pass over `a` — `ax2` never has to exist. Only the lower triangle of `ax2a` is written, since it is symmetric and `cholesky_factor` / `cholesky_apply` read nothing above the diagonal.

Largest launchable `NC` on H20 (227 KiB cap) goes **118 → 148**, bringing EP=64 with 64 redundant experts (`NC=128, NV=194`, 166 KiB) into range; it previously needed 262 KiB and could not launch.

title: [Performance][Hardware][RISC-V] Use RVV FMA in FP32Vec transcendentals and the INT4 GEMM
body:
## Purpose

GCC does not contract explicit RVV intrinsic calls into FMAs, so hand-written `vfmul` + `vfadd` pairs cost two instructions and two dependent FP latencies.

**1. FP32Vec8/16 `exp()` and `er()`** — evaluate Horner with `vfmadd_vv`, one instruction per step instead of two. `er()` also folds `1 + p*|x|` into `vfmadd_vf` and `1 - poly*exp` into `vfnmsac_vv`. `exp()`'s inner loop drops from 22 to 18 vector instructions; the polynomial itself from 10 to 5. `tanh()` is unchanged — it contains no multiply-add of its own and improves only via the `exp()` it calls.

**2. INT4 GEMM** — the weight zero-point is loop-invariant in K, so

    `sum_k a_k * (b_k - zb) = sum_k a_k * b_k - zb * sum_k a_k`

## Purpose

Related to #48680.

Weight loading currently forces `max_split_size_mb=20` for both the default CUDA caching allocator and the CuMem allocator used by sleep mode. The limit helps the default allocator avoid pinned split remainders, but it has the opposite effect inside a live `torch.cuda.MemPool`: differently-sized conversion buffers cannot reuse larger cached blocks, while the pool cannot reclaim fully free segments under pressure (pytorch/pytorch#159674). Those buffers remain stranded until the pool context exits and can OOM model loading first.

This revision preserves the default/user allocator split policy when CuMem is enabled, allowing the live pool to reuse varied conversion buffers. Non-CuMem loading retains the existing 20 MiB policy.

title: [DeepSeek-V4] Offload fp8 wo_a dequant to GPU to speed up weight loading
body:
When SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM is disabled, the fp8 `wo_a` weights are dequantized to bf16 at load time via `_dequant_fp8`. This ran on the host because the checkpoint tensors are loaded on CPU, making weight loading CPU-bound and very slow for large models like DeepSeek-V4 (the dequant is a single-threaded elementwise multiply over large tensors while the GPUs sit idle).

Move the elementwise multiply to the current CUDA device when available and move the result back to the input device, so downstream weight-loading behavior is unchanged while the heavy math is GPU-accelerated. Using `torch.cuda.current_device()` keeps this correct under tensor parallelism where each rank binds to its own device.
